title: band_world restates band_width's formula, against the file's own ONE-definition convention
detail: band_world is a restated copy of band_width ÷ scale (same 2.2 factor, same BUNDLE_EXTRA_WIDTH term) — exactly the drift pattern band_width's comment prohibits. A future band_width tune silently desyncs detour clearances from drawn widths.
recommended_fix: Define band_world as band_width(v, tier, count) / max(v.scale, 0.0001) so the 7.1 band formula stays single-source.

title: draw_glow_edge recomputes wire_path_compute per edge instead of threading the shared paths slice
detail: Four of five path consumers (draw_bundles/draw_packets/draw_selection/draw_crisis_outlines) thread draw_world's one-per-frame paths slice; draw_glow_edge re-derives the path locally (and duplicates the band_w line in both branches). Output is identical (pure function) but the plumbing pattern is inconsistent and recomputes per DAG edge when flags flip on.
recommended_fix: Pass the paths slice into draw_glow_edge like the other consumers and index paths[bi]; hoist the shared band_w computation above the branch.

title: Lane-stripe composite block duplicated between legacy and variant branches in draw_bundles
detail: The 7.1 bird's-eye hint composite (0.72/0.28 toward the tier color) now exists twice in draw_bundles. The math is deterministic and pixel-identical from either call site, so the duplication is not required for golden byte-identity; a future lane-read change must touch both copies.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared helper (e.g. lane_stripe_colors(v, col) -> [3]rl.Color) used by both branches; the legacy branch stays byte-identical since the computation is unchanged.
